title: performance canary: automatic traffic-shifting and hysteresis rollout guards
author: Evelyn Cho
description: Motivation: We've seen intermittent small latency regressions during model rollouts that cause noisy false-positive canary alerts and aggressive traffic rollback. This PR implements an automatic traffic-shifting controller with hysteresis and multi-metric gating to make canary rollouts more robust. Key behaviors: 1) gradual traffic shift (0 -> 100%) in configurable steps with delay between steps; 2) hysteresis windows to require sustained regressions before triggering rollback; 3) multi-metric gating that combines p50/p95 latency, tail-percentile CPU/GPU utilization, and error-rate; 4) adaptive step sizing that reduces step size when variance is high; 5) emergency kill-switch and manual override APIs. Includes feature flag to enable adaptive mode per-customer and per-deployment. Changes are focused in perf-canary detector, rollout controller, and metrics evaluation pipeline. See checklist and testing below.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz (2026-02-19): Nice work. Two areas: make sure the stepper respects per-customer capacity limits (we had an incident where traffic steps overloaded a dedicated pool), and add a metric that tracks step success rate over time.
Evelyn Cho (2026-02-19): Reply: added capacity check and step_success metric (see multi_metric_gating.go). Also added helm value to cap max step for Dedicated pools.
Priya Nair (2026-02-20): Request changes: hysteresis window default looks long for low-latency endpoints (default 5m). Suggest making defaults per-tier: low-latency=1m, standard=5m, bulk=15m.
Evelyn Cho (2026-02-20): Reply: added tiered defaults and annotation so customers can override. Updated docs and tests to include tiered scenarios.
Ben Carlson (2026-02-21): Approve after minor comments addressed. Please ensure observability shows a time-series for "step_delay" and per-step metrics so SRE can debug rollouts.
Evelyn Cho (2026-02-22): Added dashboard panel and instrumented step_delay in controller. Pushed final fixes.

Marco Ruiz (2026-02-24): Final approval. Ran canary sim locally with noise injection; behavior looks stable. Recommend gradual rollout to 10% of customers behind feature flag before global enablement.
testing_notes: Unit tests added for hysteresis logic and stepper. Integration test simulates noisy latency and verifies adaptive step-down behavior. E2E simulation covers: clean rollout, transient spike (should tolerate), sustained regression (should rollback), and over-capacity (should cap and pause rollout). Bench harness ran 50 simulated rollouts with noise; observed rollback rate drop from 8% -> 2% compared to baseline.
release_notes: Add automatic traffic-shifting controller for perf canaries with hysteresis and multi-metric gating. Default rollouts are safer with adaptive step sizing and tiered hysteresis. Feature behind feature-flag; enable per-deployment via helm values.
changelog_entry: perf(canary): auto traffic-shift + hysteresis rollout guards (feat)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfiguration could delay rollback on real regressions. Mitigation: feature-flag gated, default conservative settings, per-customer caps, and emergency kill-switch. We will monitor step_success and rollback_rate dashboards for first 2 weeks.
notes_for_ops:
- Enable via helm flag perfCanary.autoTrafficShift=true for canary-enabled clusters.
- Default conservative settings applied to existing customers.
- To rollback feature: set perfCanary.autoTrafficShift=false and call /api/v1/rollouts/<id>/abort.
- Dashboards: observability/dashboards/perf_canary_rollout.json includes step metrics, step_delay, step_success_rate, and rollback_count.
examples: Docs updated with an example rollout config and recommended values for low-latency/standard/bulk workloads (see docs/perf-canary/auto-traffic-shift.md).
ci_reruns: integration-tests retried once due to flaky GPU sim; subsequent runs passed
estimated_impact: Expected to reduce false-positive rollback events during rollouts (observed 6 percentage point reduction in sim).
notes: Will enable feature-flag for 10% of dev clusters next week and monitor. If metrics look good after 2 weeks, schedule broader enablement and update release notes to customers.
